collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager always leaves the evening fire first, and a friend asks if something is wrong: explain, or just say goodnight.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Every evening, (subject) leaves the fire first. (subject.He/she) eats, listens for a while, and then quietly gets up and goes to bed while everyone else is still talking. Tonight (friend) catches up with (subject.him/her) on the path. "Is something wrong? Don't you like us?"

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "I like you all very much," says (subject). "I just run out of people by about this time. Then I need quiet." (friend) thinks about this. "Like a fire running out of wood?" "Exactly like that." The next evening, when (subject) gets up to go, (friend) gives (subject.him/her) a small wave across the fire. Nobody asks again.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Nothing's wrong," says (subject). "Goodnight." (friend) isn't quite satisfied, but lets (subject.him/her) go. A few days later (friend) leaves the fire early too, just to see what it's like. The quiet on the path is lovely. (friend.He/she) understands, a bit. (friend.He/she) still prefers the fire.
